title: Rod-based Fabrication of Customizable Soft Robotic Pneumatic Gripper Devices for Delicate Tissue Manipulation
protocol: Place a container for mixer on a weighing scale and tare it.
Pour parts A and B of the silicone-based elastomer in the container with a 1:1 weight ratio.
Cover the container and measure the total weight.
Place the container and material into a centrifugal mixer.
Adjust the weight balance on the mixer to the weight measured previously.
Set the mixing mode to 2,000 rpm for 30 sec.
Set the de-aeration mode to 2,200 rpm for 30 sec.
Mix the elastomer components thoroughly to achieve uniform curing.
Click on "Sketch" on the top left corner to open a "Sketch" window.
Click on the "Sketch" button on the top left corner of the toolbar to draw a rectangular base of chamber component.
Click on the "Smart Dimension" feature, which is located beside the "Sketch" button, to define sketch dimensions.
Ensure that the sketch is fully defined and exit the sketch when done.
Click on the "Features" window.
Click on "Extruded Boss/Base" feature to extrude selected contours in the Y-direction.
Click on the top surface of the model to preselect the sketch plane.
Sketch a rectangle and define the dimensions as described.
Click on the "Features" window.
Click on "Extruded Cut" feature to extrude cut a cavity for casting elastomers.
Ensure that the wall thickness is 2.5 mm.
Right-click on the surface on the Y-direction of the opening area.
Click on "Normal to" to normalize to that surface.
Next, click on the "Sketch" window to draw a rectangle for chamber component as described in steps 2.1.1.2 and 2.1.1.3.
Click on the "Features" window.
Then, click on "Extruded Boss/Base" feature to extrude the chamber component in the Y-direction.
Preselect the sketch plane in the negative X-direction on the model surface.
Create a rectangle in the "Sketch" window.
Click on the "Features" window.
Select "Extruded Boss/Base" feature to extrude the contour in the negative X-direction.
Preselect the top surface of the gripper component as the sketch plane.
Create a shape for the gripper in the "Sketch" window.
Exit the sketch when dimensions are fully defined.
Click on the "Features" window again.
Select "Extruded Cut" to create a cavity in the gripper component for casting elastomers.
Ensure the wall thickness is 2.5 mm.
Create a rectangle in the "Sketch" window on the top surface of the chamber piece.
Click on the "Features" window.
Select "Extruded Cut" to create a connection between the chamber and gripper components.
Create 1.5 mm diameter circles on the surface of the chamber piece in the positive X-direction.
Click on the "Features" window once more.
Select "Extruded Cut" to create channels for wire rods insertion.
Ensure the holes do not cut through the gripper component.
Draw a sealing mold with a cavity that is 1 mm larger than the outer dimensions of the gripper chamber component in a CAD file.
Create a rectangle on the top plane using the "Sketch" window.
Extrude selected contours in the Y-direction by clicking on the "Features" window and selecting "Extruded Boss/Base."
Click on the top face of the model to preselect the sketch plane, then sketch another rectangle with defined dimensions as specified.
Use the "Features" window and select "Extruded Cut" feature to cut a cavity for casting elastomers.
Ensure the wall thickness is 2.5 mm during the cutting process.
Save each mold piece as a .STL file for 3D printing.
Load the .STL file into the 3D printer with a resolution of 30 µm and print the mold pieces.
Remove any support material on the mold pieces after printing.
Wash the mold pieces with water to clean them.
Insert two 3D-printed chamber-blocks on the left and right side of the chamber component to generate a sealed chamber with pneumatic channels connected to it.
Insert two 1.5 mm-diameter titanium wire rods through the chamber.
Maintain a 2 mm distance from the gripper tips to create pneumatic channels.
Pour the elastomeric mixture into the mold to fill the gripper component.
Ensure there are no visible air bubbles present in the mixture.
Place the mold into an oven for curing at 60 °C for 10 min.
Remove the mold and wire rods from the cured elastomer once complete.
Place a 3D-printed gripper-block on top of the gripper component to create the chamber.
Insert the wire rods to block holes in the wall of the mold.
Pour the elastomeric mixture into the mold to fill the remaining part of the chamber component.
Ensure there are no visible air bubbles trapped in the mold.
Cure the part at 60 °C for 10 min.
Remove the mold and gripper-block once the elastomer is cured.
Demold the fully cured gripper with chamber structure.
Pour the elastomeric mixture into the sealing mold and cure it at 60 °C for 10 min.
Brush a layer of elastomeric material on the cured 2.5 mm sealing layer.
Place the cured gripper with chamber structure on top of the coated sealing layer.
Bond the two pieces together to seal the chamber component filled with air.
Cure the entire structure fully at 60 °C for 15 min.
Demold the fully cured soft robotic gripper device.
Design handling tools using CAD software and save in .STL file.
Load the .STL file in the 3D printer and print mold pieces.
Peel off any support material on the tools after printing is completed.
Wash the tools with water.
Insert the gripper into the manual control handling tool.
Cover the opening area of the manual control handling tool with a movable rectangular cap.
Insert a movable piston to facilitate chamber compression in the manual control handling tool.
Insert the gripper and linear actuator into the robotic control handling tool.
Cover the opening area of the robotic control handling tool with a movable rectangular cap.
Evaluate the functionality of the soft gripper by performing gripping tests with a jumper wire.
Place a jumper wire on the table.
Adjust the gripper so that the wire is in between the two gripper arms.
Move the movable piston to compress the chamber to actuate the gripper arms to hold the wire.
Hold and move the wire to a box located 20 cm away from its original location.
Place a calibrated force sensing resistor between the two jaws of the gripper.
Ensure the gripper jaws grip on the sensing area.
Compress the chamber to actuate the gripper arms to grip on the force sensing resistor.
Measure the maximum grip compressive forces that the soft single-actuatable-arm and double-actuatable-arm pneumatic grippers can generate.
Cut out the individual elastomeric gripping jaws from a soft double-actuatable-arm pneumatic gripper.
Insert the forceps tips into the pneumatic channels of the elastomeric gripping jaws.
Place a calibrated force sensing resistor between the two jaws of the forceps.
Measure the compressive forces generated by elastomer-coated forceps and forceps during a simulated nerve surgery conducted by a neurosurgeon.
